segmenti.tekst: إن الحمد لله نستعينه تعالى ونستغفره ونستهديه، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فهو المهتد ومن يضلل فأولئك هم الخاسرون، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده وحبيبه وخليله وصفيه من خلقه، أدى الأمانة وبلغ الرسالة ونصح الأمة وكشف الله به الغمة وجاهد في الله حق جهاده حتى أتاه اليقين، صلى الله عليه وعلى الصحابة أجمعين ومن تبعه بإحسان واقتفى أثره إلى يوم الدين.
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we seek His help, the Exalted, and ask His forgiveness and guidance. We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides is rightly guided, and whomever He leaves astray – those are the losers (cf. Al-A'raf 7:178). I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant, His beloved, His close friend and His chosen one among His creation. He fulfilled the trust, conveyed the message, gave sincere counsel to the ummah – through him Allah removed the gloom – and strove for Allah as He deserves, until certainty (death) came to him. May Allah bless him and all the companions, and those who follow him in excellence and tread in his footsteps until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: أَلَا إِنَّ أَصْدَقَ الْكَلَامِ كَلَامُ اللَّهِ، وَخَيْرَ الْهَدْيِ هَدْيُ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، وَشَرَّ الْأُمُورِ مُحْدَثَاتُهَا
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, the truest speech is the speech of Allah, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the worst of matters are the newly invented ones (from a hadith, Muslim).

segmenti.tekst: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ
segmenti.prevod: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102)

segmenti.tekst: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا ثُمَّ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: “O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul, created from it its mate and spread from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the ties of kinship. Indeed, Allah is ever watchful over you.” (An-Nisa 4:1). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: The greatest praise and thanks belong to the Lord of the worlds. We send the most beautiful and most complete blessings and greetings of peace upon His best servant who ever walked this Earth, the seal of all the prophets and our model in goodness, Muhammad, alayhis-salatu was-salam (peace and blessings be upon him),

upon his noble family, his virtuous companions, and all the believers who steadfastly walk the path of truth until the Day of Judgment. Amin. We bear witness that there is no true deity worthy of worship except Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala (blessed and exalted is He), and we bear witness that Muhammad, alayhis-salam, is His servant and final Messenger.

In Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, we seek refuge from the evil of our souls and from our bad deeds. Of Him we ask guidance and mercy, in His Jannah (Paradise) we hope, of His Jahannam (Hellfire) we are afraid. Whomever the Exalted leaves astray, no one besides Him can show him the Straight Path, and whomever the Exalted grants the light of guidance, that guidance suffices him for complete victory and complete success both in this world and in the world to come.

My respected brothers, esteemed members of this beautiful, fine and new congregation, there is no doubt that the guidance of Muhammad, alayhis-salam, is the most complete guidance, and there is no doubt that he, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), lived the most complete, the best, the most dignified life that a man, a human being, can live.
And he conveyed that guidance of his to his companions, so that it would reach us. He taught them to be chaste, honorable, brave, to be diligent, to be hardworking, independent.

Because for a person to succeed and to be a good servant of Allah, he must conduct himself according to these instructions and these guidelines. And since Allah created us and we are His product, there is no doubt that He knows best which instructions we should follow, and if we follow them, we will have succeeded, we will be on top, prevailing, both in this world and in the world to come.
The Prophet himself, my brothers, longed for and asked Allah to make him a man on top, proud, successful and dignified. Well known is his supplication which the Prophet often used and recited.

A supplication recorded by Muslim in his “Sahih”, that the Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, said: “Allahumma inni as'aluka al-huda wat-tuqa wal-'afafa wal-ghina.” O my Allah, I ask You for guidance, and piety, and chastity, and self-sufficiency. Four things.

And like all prophetic speech – with few words it says much, or rather, it says everything – these four things, my brothers, encompass everything that is good and everything we need in order to achieve complete success and prevalence, and to be servants of Allah who are on top, both with regard to this world and with regard to the Hereafter.

As for the Hereafter, it is clear: the one who enters the religion fully, who accepts the religion completely, conducts himself by Allah's guidelines, will live a good life, because Allah revealed and decreed that when He said: “Whoever does good, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life,

and on the Day of Judgment We will reward them according to the best of what they used to do.” So here is a promise of two rewards, both worldly and otherworldly. However, this transient material world too, this dunya, has been left for us to be vicegerents in it.

To be on top, to be dignified. Not to be despised, not to be humiliated, not to be at the bottom. That is why the believer who holds fast to the religion will surely succeed in this. And it is in this that we should look for today's answers about the condition of Muslims, both in the world and locally.

When we look at the situation, we will see that the results are not such that Muslims are on top, prevailing, dignified; that they are not proud, and so on. However, there is no doubt that we, in fact, are not lagging behind the West, as some would like to say – we are lagging behind Islam, that is, we have strayed rather far from our religion and our success.

In a concise hadith, as a universal rule of our religion, which brings us to be dignified with regard to this world, the Prophet, alayhis-salam, says, as it came in the hadith in Bukhari – the Prophet, alayhis-salam, says: “The upper hand is better than the lower hand.”

And he himself continues the speech and explains his words, saying: “The upper hand is the one that gives, that bestows, and the lower hand is the one that takes and receives.” What is asked of us – the religion encourages it, Allah commands it of us – is that we be diligent, honorable and hardworking when it comes to this world. That toward Allah we have a relationship of humility, modesty, submissiveness and servitude, but that toward one another, toward other creatures, we have relationships of equality.

That the spine does not bend before a creature, but only before the Creator. This does not mean that we should not be gentle, benevolent, kind, but it means, my brothers, that Islam emphasizes that its servants should be friends, not sycophants; that they should be brothers, not subjects; that they should be on the same level, not flatterers and slaves, and so on.

That is why this matter also clearly illuminates for us that what is asked of the believer, of all people without exception, whoever is able, is to be a hardworking, diligent servant of Allah, to live from the work of his own hands, to earn, to contribute, to strengthen himself and his family first of all, and then to benefit his community.

He is not a true believer, not a complete believer, who takes these things and accepts them lightly: “I can stay in bed till noon, let Dad give me money for going out in town, as long as I'm comfortable, I don't have to do anything, I can be that lower hand that takes and receives, it's great for me, easy.”

The believer, whatever job he has to find, if he cannot find another, better one, that should be his goal, and he should be among those who are open and direct toward Allah, not shying away from halal work. The Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, says in a hadith in Bukhari: that a man takes a rope and goes to some hill, loads up a bundle of firewood, then comes down and sells it, and thereby feeds himself and his family, is better for him than asking people – whether they will give him or refuse him.

The believer does not shy away from halal work. If it means sweating at 40 degrees, or working in the rain, or this or that, but it is halal, and there is nothing better and nothing nicer, the believer should accept it with both hands. And he should know that this way, if he is dignified, if he is independent of people and lives from his own hands, he is a good servant of Allah, an obedient servant of Allah, and that such work of his, in which he is independent,

and honorable, and chaste, and honest, and of good character, and dignified, is with Allah an act of worship, with Allah a good deed. The Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, says in [unclear] a hadith in Muslim: four dinars. He says: a dinar that you spend in the way of Allah,

and a dinar with which you free a slave, and a dinar that you give to a poor person, and a dinar that you spend on your family. What do you think, which is the most valuable? He says: the most valuable dinar is the one you spend on your family.
The most valuable dinar. This clearly shows what the religion asks of us: to be decent people, to be real men, to have honor, and then to go after halal provision. To go after halal provision.

However, my brothers, this upper hand, which we are asked to be – that we be the ones who contribute, give, bestow – is conditioned by one very important thing, and that is that this upper hand be upon halal wealth.

There is no good at all, no reputation at all, no barakah (blessing), no honor, no glory, no sweetness in the one who earns in a haram way. Even if afterwards you hear: “Wallahi, he donated, gave, contributed, gave scholarships, helped, built, endowed a waqf” – in vain, my brothers, wallahi in vain, my brothers. Allah does not accept haram wealth. Perhaps by what he donated and gave from his haram wealth, well, perhaps he cleansed himself, so that there is not so much haram with him, but there is no reward as such from Allah. The Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, says in a hadith in Bukhari, in a hadith in Muslim,

he says: “Indeed, Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure.” At the end of this hadith, my brothers, the Prophet, alayhis-salatu was-salam, mentions a man – a man who is dirty and dusty, who is tired from a long journey,

who raises his hands toward Allah and says: “Ya Rabbi, ya Rabbi” – supplicating to Allah in trial, in hardship, in a state in which Allah usually accepts supplications. But the Prophet says: his drink is from haram, his food is from haram, his clothing is from haram, he has been nourished on haram – he says, so how can Allah respond to him?

“How can Allah respond to him?” – this sentence must be an alarm in our lives, so that we check well and pay close attention to where our wealth comes from. Is it pure, or is it perhaps soiled, smeared, haram?

So that perhaps, as I sometimes hear in our conversations, a person has, and drives, uses, wears, everything alhamdulillah, but there is no sweetness. There is no barakah, there is no happiness. Let him check whether his wealth is one hundred percent safe.

So the believer is asked to be the upper hand. But if he can do so in the halal; if he cannot in the halal, my brothers, it is better and more honorable for him to live like a beggar, and even to be that lower hand, with something of humiliation and [unclear] in this world, but not to go into that red zone, that haram wealth.

Especially, my brothers, today the struggle for halal wealth is a great struggle and a great jihad. Today the times are such that haram wealth is very easily accessible. That sometimes even the state system and the laws push you to fiddle something, to cheat, to lie, to twist things, and so on.

It is easier to live like that. The one who strives today to be only on the halal, watches where it comes from, is afraid: “I won't, this is not safe for me like this” – generally lives a hard, wallahi a hard life. As if he is holding a live coal: it burns him, but he must not let it go.

On the other hand, this is the time the Prophet foretold, in a hadith in Bukhari, when he said: “A time will come to people when they will not care where their wealth comes from” – halal or haram, he doesn't care. What matters is that it comes, what matters is that it lands in the account, comes in, all the rest is fine.

And unfortunately, sometimes we have people who are believers, who are perhaps even regular members of the congregation, and perhaps even some umrah, perhaps even some hajj, but when you hear how lightly he treats the way his wealth comes to him, he says: “Well, everyone does it, that's how the state is, what are you talking about now, why are you lecturing here?”

However, that is not an excuse with Allah. This is not an excuse with Allah – wallahi, even if all the hajjis and imams, and muftis, imams, hafizes, teachers, all stole and lied, let alone everyone else – that must not be proof for us, so that I say: “Well, they do it [unclear].”

No, no… Each goes into his own grave, each into his own qabr, and each will speak to Allah individually, without intermediary or interpreter, and will be asked about what he does. And he will be asked about what he does. Today it is very easy to find a person living a comfortable life.

You see him, he has some job, he works, and this and that. But he says: “Wallahi, I've arranged some extra income for myself, as if I'm somehow a bit ill, either mentally or physically, well, I've arranged that. I grabbed some welfare benefit, I got that sorted. I transferred the car to someone else so it's not registered in my name, I fiddled something,” and he tells me: “I'm enjoying life, two salaries.”

You can deceive a man, wallahi, and the state system – no problem. But you cannot deceive yourself. If you question yourself objectively, honestly and directly, as the Prophet said, if you consult your heart, you will see: “Wallahi, I lied. Wallahi, I fiddled that a bit.

I deceived someone. I signed something that is not true,” and so on and so on. You will not deceive yourself. Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, says: a person knows himself best, even if he says to someone [unclear] – he knows himself best.

He knows himself most. That is why, my brothers, a person today especially should be Allah's real, true believer, His servant, a mujahid who strives at any cost that not a single dinar of haram comes to him – through lies, deceit, bribery, through this or that.

If you have a right to something that the state gives, or an individual, or institutions, or an association, or a charity, whatever, however – you have the right, you meet the conditions – if you want, take it, no problem, you will be the lower hand, but take it if you want. However, if you have no right, if you know that it comes in this or that way, do not allow yourself, for an extra 200, 300, 500, 1,000 euros, or more or less, to disgrace yourself before Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, and to humiliate yourself.

Today you may have some witnesses of your own, perhaps you will have some collaborators of your own, you will have some connections of your own, you will have some friends and backing of your own, but you will come to the Day of Judgment. Then, when Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, causes our mouths and our eyes to be sealed, and our skin and our hands and feet, our limbs, to speak, to speak to Allah and to testify both for us and, unfortunately, by Allah, against us, if there is anything.

That is why we ask Allah to make us among those who live an honorable, upright, honest life. We ask Allah to grant us strength so that, even if everyone made use of some haram, we, alone with ourselves, stand before Allah and say: “My Lord, I will not take this, for Your sake, for Your pleasure, for the reward in Jannah, because You have decreed for me that I must not take this.”

We ask Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, to forgive us our weaknesses, sins and shortcomings. We ask Him to admit us into Jannah, us, our families, all Muslims. Finally, we ask Allah to help Islam and the Muslims, especially the oppressed, wherever they may be. We ask Allah to make us on top, victorious, dignified. We ask Allah, tabaraka wa ta'ala, for guidance, we ask for mercy, we ask for Jannah. Amin.
